# nics

Network interfaces attach an instance to a subnet.

## GET /v1/instances/{instance_id}/nics

Operation `instance_nic_list`.

Every network interface attached to one instance. The nested spelling of `GET /v1/nics?instance=<uuid>`, and the discoverable one: the instance is a path segment, so there is no selector to omit and no `400 MissingScope` on the common path.

Paginated per convention 3: `limit` (default 50, capped at 500), `page_token`, and `sort_by`. Only `id_ascending` is accepted, because `nic/in_instance/` is keyed by the NIC id. Unlike the flat form there is no residual filter, so a page under `limit` with no `next_page` really is the end of the collection.

Cursors are not interchangeable with the flat collection's even though both can walk that index: the two bind different endpoint identities, so a token cannot cross between them when their selectors diverge under convention 4.

| Parameter | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `instance_id` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |
| `limit` | query | no | integer (uint32) | Maximum rows to return. Defaults to 50 and is clamped to 500; zero is rejected rather than treated as "default". |
| `page_token` | query | no | string | Opaque cursor from the previous response's `next_page`. Valid only for the query that produced it. A token replayed against a different selector set or sort order, or modified in any way, is a `400`; it never silently restarts the listing. |
| `sort_by` | query | no | [NameOrIdSortMode](schemas.md#nameoridsortmode) | Order the collection is walked in. Defaults to `id_ascending`. Bound into the cursor, so it cannot change part-way through a walk. |

Responses:

- `200`: successful operation, `application/json`: [ResultsPage_for_Nic](schemas.md#resultspage_for_nic)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)

## GET /v1/nics

Operation `nic_list`.

`GET /v1/nics?tenant=&project=&instance=&subnet=&ip=`. Backed by the AP-1c secondary indexes (subnet, ip, instance-membership). Returns a single-row page when `ip=` is set (IP -> NIC is unique by invariant).

Paginated per convention 3: `limit` (default 50, capped at 500), `page_token`, and `sort_by`. Only `id_ascending` is accepted, because every NIC index is keyed by the NIC id. A page under `limit` does not mean the end of the collection: selectors the chosen index did not satisfy are applied per row, so only a missing `next_page` ends the walk.

| Parameter | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `instance` | query | no | string (uuid) | Restrict to NICs attached to a single instance. Backed by the existing `nic/in_instance/<instance>/<nic>` index. |
| `ip` | query | no | string (ip) | Resolve the unique NIC owning a given IP. Backed by AP-1c's `nic/by_ip/<ip>` keyspace; returns at most one row. |
| `project` | query | no | string (uuid) | Restrict to a single project. |
| `subnet` | query | no | string (uuid) | Restrict to NICs in a single subnet. Backed by AP-1c's `nic/in_subnet/<subnet>/<nic>` keyspace. |
| `tenant` | query | no | string (uuid) | Restrict to a single tenant. |
| `limit` | query | no | integer (uint32) | Maximum rows to return. Defaults to 50 and is clamped to 500; zero is rejected rather than treated as "default". |
| `page_token` | query | no | string | Opaque cursor from the previous response's `next_page`. Valid only for the query that produced it. A token replayed against a different selector set or sort order, or modified in any way, is a `400`; it never silently restarts the listing. |
| `sort_by` | query | no | [NameOrIdSortMode](schemas.md#nameoridsortmode) | Order the collection is walked in. Defaults to `id_ascending`. Bound into the cursor, so it cannot change part-way through a walk. |

Responses:

- `200`: successful operation, `application/json`: [ResultsPage_for_Nic](schemas.md#resultspage_for_nic)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
